messages:
maria: Heads-up — incident in eu-west causing elevated error-rate on model-serving. Ops flagged it 2m ago, looks like a model-side OOM spike. Pausing any active rollouts. :rotating_light:

deploybot: AUTOMATION: rollout pause requested for release v2026.04.21-rc4. All queues frozen. (request_id=rb-2791200001)

sre_oncall_jay: Thanks. Can we pin traffic to v2026.04.20-stable for now and delay the larger rollout?

devon: +1 to pin. We should avoid full rollback unless latency persists after pin. Pinning avoids DB migration churn.

elena: My team saw KV cache growth after the new attention kernel landed. If pin doesn't help we should rollback that kernel change only.

maria: deploybot — can you create a canary hold and route 100% of traffic to stable? Need the exact commands in the thread for runbook.

deploybot: ACTIONS queued:
- create route override -> model-service -> v2026.04.20-stable
- suspend canary jobs
- annotate release v2026.04.21-rc4 as "incident-paused"
- notify oncall & owners
Command: `deploybot apply override --service model-service --version v2026.04.20-stable --reason "incident pin" --by maria`

opsbot: Incident note added: "Pinned traffic to stable after eu-west model OOM spike. Investigating kernel change and KV cache." (inc-2026-0421-001)

tim: I'll run a targeted repro in staging for the kernel change, but we should also capture GC/pool stats from the nodes. @sre_oncall_jay can you grab heap dumps?

sre_oncall_jay: On it, starting heap dumps and pprof. ETA 8m. If dumps confirm OOM at attention kernel, propose a rollback of kernel patch only and re-run canary with reduced seq len.

devon: Agree. From release notes: the kernel was optional via env FLAG_USE_NEW_KERNEL=true. If we roll back the kernel we can keep other changes in rc4. Suggest two-step plan: pin -> kernel rollback -> gradual canary.

maria: Sounds good. We'll communicate schedule to PM/CS. @deploybot after pin completes, please post a short release-note update to #release-notes-digest so customers see the pause and ETA.

deploybot: Pin complete. Override applied. Release v2026.04.21-rc4 annotated. Notifications sent to owners and #eng-sre. Posting to release-notes in 2m.

elena: I'll prepare the kernel rollback PR and mark it urgent. Will attach test matrix and expected impact.

maria: Team, plan: (1) pin traffic now, (2) collect diagnostics, (3) if confirmed rollback kernel-only, schedule out-of-window patch for 30m from now with canary at 5% then ramp. If rollback not required we'll re-evaluate at +60m. Posting this as the working runbook.

tim: +1. I'll draft a short blurb for CS explaining a paused rollout due to elevated errors; include expected 60m investigation window.

sre_oncall_jay: Heap dumps uploaded to the incident S3 bucket at s3://redwood-incidents/inc-2026-0421-001/heap-dumps/. pprof URL: https://pprof.redwood.internal/2791200001. Will update with initial findings in 10m.

maria: Thanks all. If error-rate drops after pin we keep paused and prepare rollback PR. If it doesn't drop we'll consider full rollback. Notify here before any rollback command. :thumbsup:

devon: Noted. No rollbacks without +2 approvals from eng-sre and release lead.

sre_oncall_jay: Initial pprof indicates KV cache growth correlated with the new kernel in the hot path. Likely memory fragmentation. Proceed with kernel rollback PR.

elena: PR opened: #4923 — rollback-attention-kernel (label: urgent). Tests green in staging. Requesting deploy window at +30m for a targeted kernel rollback (no data migration).

maria: Approving window. Schedule patch at 2791201800 and set canary to 5% for 10m then 50% for 10m. Keep pinned until canary stable.

deploybot: Scheduled patch job: job_id=sch-2791201234, execute_at=2791201800, actions=[rollback-kernel, canary-5, canary-50]. Will post updates when it runs.

maria: Great. I'll update internal release notes and ping CS. Thanks team.

opsbot: Follow-up reminder set for +90m to re-evaluate incident and release state.
